hook_text: 600 millimetres up to the classroom door. Four steps, or seven metres of ramp. Both, actually.
clip_script: A new classroom floor sits 600 millimetres above the playground. Stairs get most people up fast: 600 divided by a 150 riser, four equal steps, treads of 250 so a foot fits. But a learner in a wheelchair, a parent with a pram, a friend on crutches: stairs lock them out. So a ramp too, at 1 in 12, one up for every twelve along, 7 200 millimetres long, because that is what arms can push. Handrails at hand height, 900 to 1 000. A landing to rest, and one at the top so nobody opens a door standing on a step. Every number in the brief is a person it protects. Specifications say what it must be. Constraints say what limits you.
visual_style: Whiteboard side view of a plinth, four steps appearing one by one, then a long ramp line with 1:12 marked; a stick figure's hand at rail height; a landing box at the door.
pacing: The problem, the stairs numbers, the ramp numbers, the rail and landing, the one-line rule.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and measure the riser height of a staircase near you.
